behavior: CLI supplies writeRecoveryJournal by default. Initial persistence precedes even the first HTTP call, then scope and each configuration/model intent checkpoint precede mutation flags and requests.
Driver passes only a structuredClone of the metadata projection to the injected callback; it also returns that safe recovery snapshot in normal and failed report.json.
Existing explicit model snapshot copies only validated id/kind/modelId/provider/chosen; implicit preference records absence plus the actual acknowledged bindingId/revision immediately on receipt.

Preparation profile records contain id and original version/digest/enabled, intendedEnabled=false, confirmed written version/digest and restored state. Private profile definitions remain in memory and are not serialized.
Fallback records contain the actual original boolean, intended value and acknowledgement/restoration states.

Any normal checkpoint failure blocks subsequent new work. Cleanup checkpoints retain failure counts without throwing, so original end/restoreSettings continues through unchanged ownRunsStopped/ownerIdle and value/version/digest guards.

Writer uses only production-run-observability-report/.recovery.json.tmp and recovery.json, exclusive temporary create at 0600, file sync, atomic rename and directory sync. Workflow always uploads only the explicitly named recovery file alongside existing safe reports.

independentSourceReview.boundary: source-only; no duplicate tests or resources

privacy.publicArtifactsBoundary: Raw tests/patches may contain explicitly synthetic canary identifiers from tracked fixtures and public workflow identity IDs/local-only e2e DB placeholders. No production secrets, cookies, passwords, profile body or account data were used or copied. MCP envelopes and signed/download URLs are excluded.

limitations: No transaction spans the normal product API mutation and the local filesystem checkpoint. A lost API acknowledgement or SIGKILL between mutation and durable acknowledgement leaves an explicitly unconfirmed intent; it cannot invent an implicit binding receipt or prove ownership of an unacknowledged write.

This is a recovery record, not an automatic resume interface. Restoring later still requires the original normal API authorization, idle and exact version/value checks. Unknown or concurrent state must not be overwritten.
An unavailable disk or lost runner can prevent final report/upload. GHA always() attempts the existing artifact upload; this change does not establish a storage acknowledgement after runner loss.

Journal identifier grammar is deliberately narrower than arbitrary custom model strings; unsupported/private-content-like strings fail before changing configuration. All ordinary preset providers, hosted empty modelId, own subscription, API-key and actual shared API-key forms are covered by source review.
The existing owner inventory is finite/non-atomic; explicit model and fallback boolean writes retain their existing non-CAS boundary.
Only isolated Node unit/CLI fixture tests and exact patch replay ran here. No full lint/typecheck, browser, Native, database, production acceptance or PostHog ingestion is claimed.

preservedVersions.finalWhitespaceChange: Only two await indentation lines after the shared-schema fix; exact final full file test rerun retained separately.
